title: Encoded PowerShell command disables security controls and downloads malware on WORKSTATION6
summary: An encoded PowerShell command (base64 -enc) ran as SYSTEM on WORKSTATION6, launched by cmd.exe. The decoded payload disables Script Block Logging and AMSI (T1562.001), then downloads and executes code from external IP 10.10.10.5 (T1105), which is flagged as suspicious as it's outside company network ranges. This follows classic attacker TTPs for defense evasion and initial access.
evidence: Encoded PowerShell command -enc flag observed in process creation logs
Decoded command disables Script Block Logging and AMSI security controls
Downloads from external IP 10.10.10.5 flagged as suspicious (not in company ranges)
Process chain: services.exe → cmd.exe → powershell.exe (with -enc) → conhost.exe
whoami.exe execution confirms successful command execution

recommended_actions.action: Block outbound connections to IP 10.10.10.5 at firewall/proxy
Full malware scan of WORKSTATION6 with updated definitions
Review and restore any modified security policy settings (Script Block Logging, AMSI)
Check for lateral movement or persistence mechanisms on other hosts

title: Malicious service 'Updater' executes encoded PowerShell on WORKSTATION6 after network logon
summary: An attacker logged into WORKSTATION6 from 172.18.39.5, then immediately installed a malicious Windows service named 'Updater' that ran an encoded PowerShell command. The command disables script block logging and AMSI, downloads malware from 10.10.10.5, and executes it. This follows the same pattern as ALERT-001 on the same host. The user pgustavo (domain lab user) appears compromised or coerced.
evidence: New Windows service 'Updater' installed by pgustavo on WORKSTATION6 at 16:16:58
Service executed encoded PowerShell ( -enc ) that disables Script Block Logging and AMSI
Encoded command downloads malware from http://10.10.10.5 and runs downloaded code
Successful network logon by pgustavo from 172.18.39.5 at 16:16:58.212
IP 172.18.39.5 rated internal (company network)
pgustavo is a Domain user (lab) with normal host WORKSTATION5
Same user connected from WORKSTATION5 to external IP 172.18.39.6 after the logon
Prior ALERT-001 on WORKSTATION6 involved encoded PowerShell disabling security and downloading malware
MITRE techniques confirmed: T1021.002 (Remote Services), T1543.003 (Windows Service), T1569.002 (Service Execution)
related_to_prior: Continuation of ALERT-001 on WORKSTATION6 - same host, same attacker TTPs, same user pgustavo deploying additional payload after initial encoded command

recommended_actions.action: Terminate the 'Updater' malicious service on WORKSTATION6
Block outbound connections from WORKSTATION6 to 10.10.10.5 at firewall
Reset credentials for user pgustavo and audit all domain accounts for compromise
Collect full process tree and memory dump from WORKSTATION6 for forensic analysis
Check other hosts for similar 'Updater' service installation or encoded PowerShell execution

title: Encoded PowerShell beacon from WORKSTATION6 connects to external IP
summary: On WORKSTATION6, the malicious 'Updater' service (installed by user pgustavo) launched cmd.exe which invoked powershell.exe with -encoded command flag. The decoded command disables Script Block Logging and AMSI, contains nested base64, uses proxy credentials, and downloads payload from 10.10.10.5:80. This IP is flagged as suspicious (private address outside company network). The powershell session also ran whoami.exe for reconnaissance. This is part of a confirmed attack chain starting with ALERT-002 (malicious service) and ALERT-001 (encoded command disabling security controls).
evidence: powershell.exe launched as SYSTEM with -enc flag by cmd.exe (parented by services.exe) at 16:16:57
decoded command disables Script Block Logging, Invocation Logging, and bypasses AMSI
decoded command downloads from http://10.10.10.5 with nested base64 and proxy credentials
IP 10.10.10.5 rated suspicious (private address not in company network ranges)
service 'Updater' installed by pgustavo launched identical encoded powershell command at 16:16:58
powershell subsequently executed whoami.exe for reconnaissance
attack chain connects ALERT-002 (malicious service) and ALERT-001 (encoded security-disabling command)
T1071.001 confirmed: C2 over HTTP/S to external IP
T1562.001 confirmed: defense evasion via disabling logging and AMSI bypass
related_to_prior: Continues attack chain from ALERT-002 (malicious 'Updater' service) and ALERT-001 (encoded PowerShell disabling security controls), both on WORKSTATION6. This alert represents the C2 communication phase of the same intrusion.

recommended_actions.action: Terminate malicious 'Updater' service and kill active powershell processes
Block outbound connections to 10.10.10.5 at perimeter firewall
Reset credentials for user pgustavo and audit service creation
Full malware scan of WORKSTATION6 with updated definitions
Review other hosts for similar 'Updater' service installations
